title: Effects of a 4-week dual-task training program compared to guideline-based exercise therapy in individuals with chronic neck pain
summary:
Many people suffer from long-lasting neck pain, which can interfere with daily life. The aim of this study is to investigate which type of training is most effective in reducing neck pain and everyday limitations.
The study examines a four-week training program and compares three different types of training. All participants are randomly assigned to one of the three groups:

Group 1 completes a well-established exercise program including exercises to improve neck mobility, coordination, and strength.
Group 2 completes the same exercise program, combined with balance tasks and exercises that involve following moving objects with the eyes and head.
Group 3 performs only exercises that involve following moving objects with the eyes and head.

interventions.name: Guideline-based exercise program (based on the guidelines of the American Physical Therapy Association, APTA) including active exercises for mobility, coordination, and strengthening/stabilization.

Guideline-based exercise program combined with a balance task and a visuomotor task (visuomotor tracking training, VM-TT).
The eye–head tracking task has previously been used as an assessment tool.
Exclusive performance of visuomotor tracking training (VM-TT).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients with a current physiotherapy prescription
Neck pain lasting longer than three months
Exclusion criteria:
Acute lesions of the shoulder or spine (less than three weeks) that significantly limit the patient’s activities of daily living (i.e., essential activities required to meet basic physical and psychological needs are not possible)
Presence of general red flags, such as long-term use of corticosteroids, nausea, vomiting, or fever
Current use of pain medication of any kind, including non-opioids, weak opioids, and strong opioids
Recent surgery or fractures of any kind
Cervical spondyloarthrosis (classified according to ICD-10 M47.812)
Cervical neuralgia, unspecified (classified according to ICD-10 M54.2
Rheumatoid arthritis, unspecified (classified according to ICD-10 M06.9
Blindness and visual impairment (classified according to ICD-10 H54.-)
Dizziness and vertigo (classified according to ICD-10 R42)
Acute ankle sprain (supination injury) (classified according to ICD-10 S93.4)
